classes.description: A common fungal disease characterized by brown-black spots with concentric rings ('target board' pattern) initially appearing on older, lower foliage.
symptoms: Dark brown to black necrotic spots with concentric rings
Yellow chlorotic halo surrounding lesions
Lower leaves yellowing and dropping prematurely
Stem collar rot in severe cases
next_steps: Prune and safely destroy heavily infected lower leaves (do not compost).
Avoid overhead irrigation; switch strictly to drip irrigation to keep foliage dry.
Ensure wide plant spacing (at least 45-60 cm) to enhance airflow and sunlight penetration.
Apply organic copper fungicide or Trichoderma viride preventive bio-spray under agricultural supervision.

classes.description: An aggressive, fast-spreading oomycete water-mold disease that attacks foliage and green fruit in cool, humid, overcast weather.
symptoms: Irregular water-soaked, dark greasy lesions on leaves and stems
White downy fungal fuzz visible on leaf undersides during humid mornings
Rapid browning and collapse of entire foliage canopy
Greasy, firm dark brown rot on green and ripe tomato fruits
next_steps: Immediately isolate affected plants to prevent rapid field-wide dissemination.
Cease sprinkler/overhead watering immediately.
Remove and bag infected vines during dry afternoon hours.
Consult local Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK) for recommended systemic oomycete protection.

classes.description: A destructive viral disease transmitted by the whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) leading to severe stunting and aborted flower formation.
symptoms: Severe upward curling and cupping of leaflets
Interveinal yellowing (chlorosis) and reduced leaf blade size
Bushy, stunted plant architecture
Flower drop resulting in drastic yield loss
next_steps: Control whitefly vectors using yellow sticky traps (15-20 traps per acre).
Spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) or approved biological insecticides.
Rogue out and destroy severely stunted plants to avoid virus reservoir build-up.
Use insect-proof netting in seedling nursery trays.

classes.description: Vibrant, turgid green foliage showing no observable lesions, chlorosis, wilting, or insect defoliation.
symptoms: Uniform rich green color across leaf surface
Normal venation and smooth leaflet margins
Robust stem vigor and clean nodal growth
next_steps: Maintain current drip irrigation schedule matching crop stage evapotranspiration.
Continue balanced NPK fertigation schedule.
Perform routine twice-weekly scouting on lower leaf undersides.

classes.description: Fungal pathogen that targets older foliage of Solanaceous crops, reducing tuber bulking efficiency.
symptoms: Angular brown-black spots with concentric ridges
Premature defoliation of lower canopy
Dry brown lesions on stem base
next_steps: Maintain adequate nitrogen and potassium fertility to avoid plant stress.
Allow foliage to completely dry before morning cultivation.
Practice minimum 2-year crop rotation away from Solanaceae.

classes.description: The historic cause of potato famine; spreads rapidly in high humidity (>90%) and temperatures between 15-22°C.
symptoms: Water-soaked dark lesions starting from leaf tips and margins
White mildew on undersides under high humidity
Tuber rot with reddish-brown dry granular flesh beneath skin
next_steps: Kill vines 10-14 days before harvest to prevent tuber contamination at digging.
Hill up soil properly to cover tubers deeply from spore runoff.
Seek certified disease-free seed tubers for subsequent cycles.

classes.description: Robust, deep-green compound leaves without blight spots or chlorotic mottling.
symptoms: Crisp, even foliage without dark spots
Healthy floral development or vegetative canopy closure
next_steps: Maintain soil moisture at 65-75% field capacity during tuber initiation.
Monitor weather forecasts for sudden humidity spikes.

classes.description: Bacterial disease spread by splashing rain, wind-driven moisture, and handling wet plants.
symptoms: Small, circular to irregular water-soaked spots turning dark brown
Raised scabby texture on lower leaf surface
Severe leaf drop exposing fruit to sunscald
next_steps: Never work in or cultivate the field when foliage is wet from morning dew or rain.
Sterilize pruning tools between plants using 70% isopropyl alcohol.
Apply certified copper bactericide in combination with mancozeb as per agricultural extension guidelines.

classes.description: Healthy bell pepper foliage with shiny, intact dark green lamina.
symptoms: Glossy green leaves with uniform surface
Firm stem nodes and active flower buds
next_steps: Support plants with staking or trellis to prevent lodging.
Maintain uniform moisture to prevent blossom end rot.

classes.description: Airborne fungal disease that creates powdery cinnamon-brown pustules on both upper and lower leaf surfaces.
symptoms: Oval to elongate cinnamon-brown pustules (uredinia) on leaf blades
Powdery rust spores rubbing off on fingers
Leaves turning yellow and withering in heavy infestations
next_steps: Plant rust-resistant hybrids recommended for Maharashtra Kharif/Rabi seasons.
Maintain balanced fertilization; avoid excess nitrogen.
Scout whorl and ear leaves weekly.

classes.description: Vigorous maize leaves showing clean venation and sturdy whorl growth.
symptoms: Broad, smooth green leaves with unbroken midrib
No pustules, stripes, or necrotic tips
next_steps: Ensure adequate moisture during silking and tasseling phases.
Side-dress nitrogen as per soil test recommendations.
